headerDisplay:
Klares4 - Ksenia Lares4 for Homebridge

Homebridge plugin for local control of the Ksenia Lares4 panel, over HomeKit, Matter and MQTT.

Prerequisites:
  • Panel reachable on the local network
  • WebSocket interface enabled
  • A valid user PIN (4-8 digits)
footerDisplay:

name.title: Platform Name
name.description: Name shown in the Homebridge log

ip.title: Panel IP Address
ip.description: Local IP address of the Ksenia Lares4 panel

port.title: WebSocket Port
port.description: Leave empty to use 443 with HTTPS and 80 without. Set it only if the panel uses a different port.

allowInsecureTls.title: Allow Insecure TLS
allowInsecureTls.description: Turns off the check of the panel's TLS certificate and allows the legacy TLS renegotiation that most panels need (they use a self-signed certificate and old TLS settings). Use it only on a trusted local network, and only when the log asks for it.

sender.title: Client Identifier
sender.description: Name that identifies this connection on the panel (letters, digits, hyphen, underscore)

pin.title: Access PIN
pin.description: User PIN allowed to use the WebSocket API on the panel. It is stored in clear text in Homebridge's config.json: use a dedicated panel user with only the rights this plugin needs.

showAdvanced.title: Show Advanced Settings
showAdvanced.description: Unlocks the timing and network parameters. Only used by this settings form.

debug.title: Debug Mode (legacy)
debug.description: Legacy switch, the same as Log Level 2: when it is on, the level is 2 whatever Log Level says.

logLevel.title: Log Level
logLevel.description: 0: warnings and errors only. 1: connection and synchronization, the startup device summary, commands, accessories added and removed. 2: everything else too (each state change reported by the panel, per-device discovery lines, masked frames), written at info level and marked [debug], so Homebridge does not have to run in debug mode (-D).

maxSeconds.title: Cover Travel Time
maxSeconds.description: Seconds a cover needs to open or close completely. HomeKit (HAP) only: Matter shows the position the panel reports.

reconnectInterval.title: Base Reconnect Interval
reconnectInterval.description: Milliseconds before the first reconnection attempt. It doubles at every failed attempt and restarts after a complete synchronization.

heartbeatInterval.title: Heartbeat Interval
heartbeatInterval.description: Milliseconds between the keep-alive pings that detect a dead connection

commandTimeoutMs.title: Command Timeout
commandTimeoutMs.description: Maximum wait for the panel's answer to a command, thermostats included. A command still queued after this time is refused instead of being sent late.

coverStepSize.title: Cover Animation Step
coverStepSize.description: Percentage moved at each animation step while a cover travels in HomeKit. HomeKit (HAP) only.

scenarioAutoOffDelay.title: Scenario Auto-Off Delay
scenarioAutoOffDelay.description: Milliseconds before a scenario switch, or a gate, returns to Off by itself after it was triggered

exposePartialArmScenarios.title: Expose Partial-Arm Scenarios
exposePartialArmScenarios.description: When off (default), scenarios of category PARTIAL (partial arming) are not exposed to HomeKit, Matter or MQTT and cannot be run, like ARM/DISARM scenarios, which are never exposed. Turn it on only if you accept that anyone who can operate the switch (voice assistants, scenes, automations, MQTT) can partially arm the alarm without a PIN prompt.

exposeOutputs.title: Expose These Outputs Anyway
exposeOutputs.description: Outputs of a category the plugin does not recognize (GEN such as sirens, alarm bridges, indicators or door strikes; IRR irrigation; no category) are not exposed to HomeKit, Matter or MQTT and cannot be controlled. Add an output here only if it is safe to switch it from voice assistants, scenes and automations ("turn off all the lights" included). The startup log lists the hidden outputs with the exact entry to add.

outputId.title: Output ID (panel)
outputId.description: The numeric ID of the output, as printed by the startup log

exposeAs.title: Expose As
exposeAs.description: The output appears as a light (on/off), with the same ID, HomeKit identity and MQTT topic it had in 2.2.0. A row that leaves this empty means light.

exposeScenarios.title: Expose These Scenarios Anyway
exposeScenarios.description: Scenarios are exposed only when the panel lists them as generic (GEN). Scenarios with no category or an unknown one are hidden and cannot be run; list one here to expose it. Arming and disarming scenarios (ARM, DISARM) are never exposed; partial arming (PARTIAL) only with "Expose Partial-Arm Scenarios".

scenarioId.title: Scenario ID (panel)
scenarioId.description: The numeric ID of the scenario, as printed by the startup log

devicesSummaryDelay.title: Device Summary Delay
devicesSummaryDelay.description: Milliseconds to wait before the device summary is printed in the log

excludeZones.title: Excluded Zones
excludeZones.description: Numeric zone IDs (the number of zone_5 is 5) to leave out of HomeKit, Matter and MQTT

excludeOutputs.title: Excluded Outputs
excludeOutputs.description: Numeric output IDs (the number of light_37 is 37) to leave out: lights, covers, gates and thermostats

excludeSensors.title: Excluded Sensors
excludeSensors.description: Numeric DOMUS sensor IDs (hides all three readings) or sensor_system_temp_in / sensor_system_temp_out for the panel's own temperatures

excludeScenarios.title: Excluded Scenarios
excludeScenarios.description: Numeric scenario IDs to leave out

matterExposure.title: Matter Exposure by Type
matterExposure.description: Turn off a whole type of device on Matter only. HomeKit and MQTT are not affected.

matterOverrides.title: Matter Overrides per Device
matterOverrides.description: Optional per-device overrides, by Klares4 device ID. They change Matter only: HomeKit and MQTT are not affected.

deviceId.title: Device ID
deviceId.description: ID as printed by the startup log and written in klares4-devices.json (also sensor_system_temp_in / sensor_system_temp_out for the panel's own temperatures)

exposed.title: Exposed on Matter
exposed.description: Untick to hide the device from Matter only. When ticked, the device stays exposed even if its type is turned off in Matter Exposure by Type.

matterRecoveryRequests.title: Matter Thermostat Recovery Requests
matterRecoveryRequests.description: Administrative: raising the generation allows one more controlled attempt to register the thermostat as a native Matter Thermostat again.

generation.title: Generation
generation.description: An integer from 1 up. A row without a device ID or without a generation is ignored.

matterUnregisterTimeoutMs.title: Matter Endpoint Removal Timeout
matterUnregisterTimeoutMs.description: Milliseconds to wait for a removed Matter endpoint to really disappear before giving up and keeping the current name

customNames.title: Custom Names
customNames.description: Renames devices on HomeKit, MQTT and Matter. The old per-category map format is still read, but the Homebridge UI deletes it the next time you save.

deviceId.title: Device ID
deviceId.description: ID as printed by the startup log and written in klares4-devices.json. For DOMUS sensors sensor_<id> works too: the name applies to temperature, humidity and light. For the panel's own temperatures use sensor_system_temp_in / sensor_system_temp_out (the name is used as written).

target.title: Default Target Temperature
target.description: Setpoint (°C) shown while the thermostat has not reported one

min.title: Minimum Temperature
min.description: Lowest setpoint (°C). Also applied to MQTT setpoint commands.

max.title: Maximum Temperature
max.description: Highest setpoint (°C). Also applied to MQTT setpoint commands.

temperatureDefaults.title: Thermostat Temperature Defaults
temperatureDefaults.description: Setpoint range and step of the HomeKit (HAP) thermostat, also applied to setpoints received over MQTT. Matter thermostats use fixed ranges (heating 5-30 °C, cooling 16-35 °C).

enabled.title: Use DOMUS Sensors for Thermostats
enabled.description: Use the DOMUS sensors for the current temperature of the thermostats

sensorFreshnessMs.title: DOMUS Sensor Freshness (ms)
sensorFreshnessMs.description: How long a realtime thermostat reading takes precedence over the DOMUS sensor reading

manualCommandPairs.title: Thermostat Command Mapping
manualCommandPairs.description: Links a thermostat output to the thermostat ID the panel uses for commands. Written by the KSA import; usually it needs no manual editing. A pair that points to an ID the panel does not have makes every write of that thermostat fail.

manualPairs.title: Manual Sensor Mapping
manualPairs.description: Links a thermostat output to the DOMUS sensor that gives its room temperature

domusThermostat.title: DOMUS Thermostats
domusThermostat.description: How thermostats get their room temperature and which panel thermostat each one commands

enabled.title: Enable KSA Import
enabled.description: Loads the .ksa backup at startup to derive thermostat mappings and room data. Nothing is written to config.json unless "Apply to config at next start" is on.

filePath.title: .ksa File Path
filePath.description: Absolute path of the .ksa backup exported from the panel

applyAtStartup.title: Apply to Config at Next Start
applyAtStartup.description: Writes the selected sections into config.json at the next start, then switches itself off

applyDomusMappings.title: Apply Thermostat Mappings
applyDomusMappings.description: Adds the thermostat mappings of the backup that are missing. The pairs you configured are never replaced.

applyRoomMapping.title: Apply Room Mapping
applyRoomMapping.description: Uses the room names of the panel for MQTT topics when you have defined no rooms yourself. It never turns Room Mapping on.

applyCustomNames.title: Apply Custom Names
applyCustomNames.description: Adds the names of the panel for devices you have not named yourself

ksaImport.title: KSA Backup Import
ksaImport.description: Reads a .ksa backup exported from the panel to derive thermostat mappings, rooms and names

enabled.title: Enable MQTT Bridge
enabled.description: Publishes device state and availability over MQTT and, unless "Accept Commands over MQTT" is off, receives commands

commands.title: Accept Commands over MQTT
commands.description: When off, the bridge only publishes device state and availability: it does not subscribe to the .../set topics, so nothing published on the broker can operate lights, covers, thermostats or scenarios. Leave it on only if the broker requires authentication and its ACL limits who can write the .../set topics.

broker.title: MQTT Broker URL
broker.description: Full broker address with its scheme (mqtt://host:1883 or mqtts://host:8883). Prefer the Username and Password fields to credentials inside the URL.

port.title: Broker Port
port.description: Overrides the port in the broker URL. Leave it empty to use the URL's port, or the protocol default (1883 for mqtt://, 8883 for mqtts://).

clientId.title: Client ID
clientId.description: Must be unique for each Homebridge instance on the same broker. Leave empty for a random one.

topicPrefix.title: Topic Prefix
topicPrefix.description: Prefix of every published topic. It cannot contain + or #.

retain.title: Retain State Messages
retain.description: The broker keeps the last state for new subscribers (state topics; the status topic is always retained)

enabled.title: Enable Room Mapping
enabled.description: Organizes the MQTT topics by room instead of by device type. It changes every topic of the devices you map.

roomName.title: Room Name
roomName.description: Lowercase letters, digits and underscore only

generateDebugFile.title: Generate Debug File
generateDebugFile.description: Turn on to write a diagnostic file at the next restart; it switches itself off afterwards. The file is confidential: it lists your devices and the state of your alarm system. Do not attach it to a public issue; send it privately.

debugCaptureDurationMs.title: Capture Duration (ms)
debugCaptureDurationMs.description: How long the debug capture records the panel traffic (default 60000 = 60 s). Raise it to 300000 (5 min) or 600000 (10 min) on Matter-only setups where Apple Home needs minutes to respond after a child bridge restart.

items.helpvalue:
Essential settings

Enter the IP address and the PIN of the panel. The port is needed only if it is not 443 (HTTPS) or 80 (HTTP). If you do not know the IP address, check it in the network settings of the panel.

The PIN is stored in clear text in Homebridge's config.json: use a dedicated panel user with only the rights this plugin needs.

items.title: Panel IP Address
items.validationMessage: Enter a valid IP address (for example 192.168.1.100)

items.title: Access PIN
items.validationMessage: The PIN must contain only digits (4-8)

items.helpvalue:
Device preferences

Adjust how covers, thermostats and scenarios behave, without changing what is discovered.

items.title: Apply to Config at Next Start
items.description: Logs a preview and writes the selected sections into config.json, then switches itself off
After it is triggered, the switch returns to Off by itself

items.helpvalue:
How to find the IDs
  1. Start the plugin at least once
  2. In the device summary printed in the log, or in the id field of klares4-devices.json in the Homebridge storage folder, copy the exclude value of the device (the numeric ID without prefix, for example 37 for light_37; for the panel's own temperatures sensor_system_temp_in or sensor_system_temp_out)
  3. Enter it below with the + Add button

Outputs of a category the plugin does not recognize (GEN, IRR, none) and scenarios of an unknown category are hidden by default. The startup log lists them with the exact entry to add under Expose Hidden Devices.

items.title: Excluded Outputs (lights, covers, gates, thermostats)
items.description: Enter the numeric ID only, without prefix

items.title: Excluded Zones (security sensors)
items.description: Zones you do not want as contact sensors

items.title: Excluded Sensors (environmental)
items.description: Temperature, humidity and light sensors to hide. A DOMUS ID hides all three readings; for the panel's own temperatures use sensor_system_temp_in / sensor_system_temp_out

items.title: Excluded Scenarios
items.description: Scenarios you do not want to run from HomeKit, Matter or MQTT

items.helpvalue:
Fail-closed exposure

A hidden device is never exposed or controllable. Add an output or a scenario here only if it is safe to operate it from voice assistants, scenes and automations. Arming and disarming scenarios (ARM, DISARM) can never be exposed.

Matter side only

Turns off whole device types on Matter controllers (Alexa, Google Home, Apple Home over Matter) without touching HomeKit or the MQTT bridge. Useful on voice-first installations: hiding the contact zones, for example, shrinks the voice namespace and removes name ambiguity. Endpoints that are already registered are removed after 3 consecutive synchronizations.

items.title: Overrides by Device ID
items.description: Change the name or the exposure of a single device, on Matter only. HomeKit and MQTT are not affected.

items.helpvalue:
Thermostat recovery

Controlled administration only. Thermostats register as native Matter thermostats; one that an earlier version saved as a temperature sensor gets one automatic attempt at the first start. To allow one more attempt, link a thermostat device ID to a generation and raise the number. On failure the plugin falls back to the temperature sensor.

items.title: Recovery Generations by Device ID
items.description: Do not raise the number automatically at every start.

items.helpvalue:
Rename devices

One row per device: the device ID (as printed by the startup log, for example light_18) and the name. The name also changes the MQTT topic slug and the name on Matter.

MQTT bridge

Publishes device state and availability on MQTT and, if you leave commands on, receives commands from external systems (Home Assistant, Node-RED, custom automations).

Topics: {prefix}/{type}/{slug}/state, {prefix}/{type}/{slug}/set, {prefix}/status

Security: commands are not authenticated by the plugin. Use a broker with authentication and an ACL, or turn commands off.

Organize topics by room

Example: from klares4/light/ceiling to living_room/light/ceiling. Use a lowercase roomName with underscores. With room mapping on, a command is executed only through the topic of the room the device belongs to (or the room-less topic).

Advanced section

Change these parameters only if you need to. Wrong values can cause timeouts, frequent reconnections or a No Response state.

items.title: Unlock Advanced Parameters
items.description: Turn on to edit the timing and network parameters
Keep-alive ping frequency (a missing PONG drops the connection)
Wait for the answer to a command, thermostats included
Only for panels with a self-signed certificate
0 warnings and errors only, 1 normal, 2 detailed trace (no Homebridge debug mode needed)
Delay before the device list is printed

items.helpvalue:
Complete diagnostic tool

Writes a support file with:

  • the raw WebSocket messages (for the duration set in Capture Duration, 60 seconds by default)
  • the list of discovered devices
  • a snapshot of states and main commands

Important: while the capture runs, try the devices that do not work from the Ksenia app, so the trace includes the real behavior of the panel.

The file is confidential. It contains the names of your devices and the state of your alarm system (PIN, account, serial numbers and home position are masked). Do not attach it to a public issue: send it privately.

items.title: Generate Debug File at Next Start
items.description: Switches itself off after the file is written. The file is confidential: send it privately.

items.title: Capture Duration (ms)
items.description: Default 60000 (60 s). On Matter-only setups where Apple Home needs minutes to respond again, raise it to 600000 (10 min).

items.helpvalue:
Suggested procedure
  1. Turn the option on and save the configuration
  2. Restart Homebridge
  3. During the capture (Capture Duration, 60 seconds by default) test the problem devices from the Ksenia app
  4. Wait for the end-of-capture message in the log
  5. Fetch the generated file and send it privately: it is confidential

Debug file location

Default location:

~/.homebridge/klares4-debug-*.json

On macOS this is usually:

/Users/[your-username]/.homebridge/klares4-debug-*.json

The log always shows the full path of the file just created.
